title: Longest Palindromic Substring
description:
# Longest Palindromic Substring

Given a string `s`, return the longest contiguous substring of `s` that is a palindrome.

A palindrome reads the same from left to right and from right to left. The answer must be a substring, so the chosen characters must stay adjacent in the original string.

If more than one longest palindromic substring exists, return the one with the smallest starting index.

## Example 1

**Input:** `s = "babad"`

**Output:** `"bab"`

**Explanation:** `"aba"` is also length `3`, but `"bab"` starts earlier.

## Example 2

**Input:** `s = "cbbd"`

**Output:** `"bb"`

**Explanation:** The longest palindrome has even length and is centered between the two `b` characters.

## Example 3

**Input:** `s = "bananas"`

**Output:** `"anana"`

**Explanation:** The substring from index `1` to index `5` reads the same in both directions.

## Constraints

- `1 <= s.length <= 1000`
- `s` consists only of digits and English letters.

solutions.name: Length-Descending Brute Force
solutions.description:
## Approach

Try candidate substring lengths from longest to shortest. For each length, scan starts from left to right and validate the substring with two pointers. The first valid candidate is the required leftmost longest palindrome.

## Key Insight

This baseline is intentionally simple: it separates the definition of a palindrome from the search order. Searching by descending length makes the first success globally optimal, and scanning starts left to right enforces the tie rule.

## Complexity Analysis

There are `O(n^2)` candidate substrings, and each validation may scan `O(n)` characters, so the time complexity is `O(n^3)`. The two-pointer check stores only indices, so the space complexity is `O(1)`.

solutions.name: Expand Around Center
solutions.description:
## Approach

Every palindrome has a center. For each index, expand once as an odd-length center and once as an even-length center between two characters. Keep the best range seen so far, updating only when a strictly longer palindrome appears.

## Key Insight

A palindrome is determined by its center and radius. Expanding outward turns the problem into checking matching pairs, and strict updates preserve the earliest answer when two longest palindromes tie.

## Complexity Analysis

There are `2n - 1` centers, and each expansion may scan across the string, so the time complexity is `O(n^2)`. Only the best start and length are stored, giving `O(1)` space.

solutions.name: Dynamic Programming Table
solutions.description:
## Approach

Let `palindrome[start][end]` mean that `s[start..end]` is a palindrome. Fill ranges from shorter to longer so the inner range `start + 1..end - 1` is known before the outer range is evaluated.

## Key Insight

A substring is a palindrome when its two endpoint characters match and the inside substring is also a palindrome. Length `1` and length `2` ranges are the base cases that make the recurrence start cleanly.

## Complexity Analysis

The table has `O(n^2)` entries, and each entry is computed in constant time. The time complexity is `O(n^2)`, and the table uses `O(n^2)` space.

solutions.name: Manacher's Algorithm
solutions.description:
## Approach

Transform the string by inserting separators so odd and even palindromes are handled uniformly. Maintain the rightmost palindrome currently known and mirror radius information across its center to avoid rechecking characters.

## Key Insight

When a center lies inside the current right boundary, its mirror center already describes part of its radius. Only the unmatched suffix beyond the boundary needs fresh expansion, which makes the total expansion work linear.

## Complexity Analysis

Each transformed character moves the right boundary at most once, so the time complexity is `O(n)`. The transformed array and radius array use `O(n)` space.

solutions.name: Reversed String LCS with Index Guard
solutions.description:
## Approach

Compute the longest common substring between `s` and `reverse(s)`, but accept a match only when the reversed match maps back to the same original indices. This index guard removes false positives where a common substring is not actually mirrored in place.

## Key Insight

A palindrome appears unchanged when the whole string is reversed, but ordinary common substrings can also appear in unrelated positions. The original-start check is the difference between a tempting shortcut and a correct algorithm.

## Complexity Analysis

The dynamic-programming table compares every pair of positions in `s` and `reverse(s)`, so the time complexity is `O(n^2)`. The table stores `O(n^2)` suffix lengths.
